correctness.rationale: For all integers n>=2, acyclic K2n orientations are exactly S_+^n union S_-^n, and signs give unique centered Euclidean vertex coordinates. The exact norm identity decomposes hub differences and leaf differences, supporting every exponent in the nine-kernel inclusion-exclusion polynomial; removing N diagonal terms and dividing by two is exact. Integer parity, maximum and minimum are established. Same-branch CLT uses covariance 2[[8/9,4/9],[4/9,8/9]], resulting in hub eigenweights 2/3 and 2/9 and leaf average 4/3. Opposite-branch mean hub difference (2/3,-2/3) gives n^2 coefficient 2/9 and n^(3/2) variance 16/81. Exceptional and diagonal pair masses are exponentially small. The independent standard-library checker reproduces 1,085,463 unordered pairs at n=2..6, exact transfer convolution and first moments at n=2..12. Finite computation is corroborative, not a proof of infinite limits.

originality.rationale: A complete Euclidean pairwise-distance polynomial and its conditional two-scale limits are distinct from the already published one-vertex norm histogram, covariance, outer radius, and acyclic-orientation/face classification. Same-object results and closest abstracts were compared by implication. The known diameter and mean-square moment are expressly credited as consistency checks; the present novelty assessment applies only to the full two-point distribution and its non-Gaussian/Gaussian two-branch limits. Residual risk of an unindexed equivalent multivariate enumeration remains.
residual_risks: A separately published or unindexed joint distribution of indegree vectors or lonesum sign-word pairs could imply the exact coefficient formula.

General two-sample mixture asymptotic principles may make the method unsurprising, but the complete natural metric invariant and explicit two-scale constants are not implied by located earlier claims.
The web and semantic research index cannot establish absolute priority.

value.rationale: The complete Euclidean vertex-chord distribution is a canonical metric invariant for an established infinite family, computable in polynomial rather than exponential time. Unlike the known radial shells, covariance and diameter, it distinguishes conditional near chords of order n with a shifted weighted chi-square law from opposite-branch chords of order n^2 with Gaussian n^(3/2) fluctuations. A genuine half/half two-scale metric clustering emerges upon adding the second hub to a star. This is a mathematically motivated, non-subsumed structural phenomenon rather than an arbitrary finite parameter or a minor table increment.
